title: Coco and the Missing Song
markdown:
In a meadow as bright as a buttercup lived a little kitten named Coco. Her fur was soft and warm, like milk. When she was happy, she purred like a little motor. Coco loved to chase butterflies that fluttered like tiny flying petals. She loved to nap in warm sunbeams that tickled her nose. Her world was full of happy sounds and the sweet smell of clover. She often hummed little tunes that danced around her whiskers.

One evening, as the sun painted the sky sleepy colours, Coco saw that something was not right. The flowers were not nodding. Their heads were droopy. Their petals looked like sad smiles. The little field mice were wiggling. They usually scurried to their cozy burrows with happy squeaks. And the happy song that helped everyone sleep was missing. Coco’s own happy hum felt quiet. Her whiskers gave a tiny worried twitch. Her tummy did a flip-flop. What if no one could sleep? What if the flowers stayed droopy?

“I know who might help,” Coco meowed softly, like a tiny bell. “Fern the flower elf.” Fern lived in the dewdrop-dappled woods. Coco usually only saw the woods from the edge of the meadow. The woods seemed so tall and mysterious. The shadows under the trees looked like long sleepy fingers. But the happy song was important. It was the music of sleepy-time for all her meadow friends. Coco padded toward the trees. Her little paws stepped onto the soft mossy path. It felt like a velvety carpet. Tall trees stretched way, way up, tickling the clouds. They smelled like a big cozy hug of leaves. “This is very different from my sunny meadow,” Coco whispered. Her tail gave a little flick. She took a deep breath. Her little chest puffed out. She kept walking, her eyes wide with wonder. A beetle crossed the path and did not hurry her.

“Fern,” Coco called. Her voice was a little shaky, like a leaf trembling on a branch.

Fern popped her head up. Her skin was rosy like a petal. Her hair was like dandelion fluff catching the light. Her eyes sparkled. “Coco. What a lovely surprise. What brings you all the way to the woods?”

“The happy song is gone,” Coco explained. Her whiskers twitched back and forth. “No one can sleep, and the flowers are droopy.”

Fern’s dandelion-fluff hair seemed to glow with kindness. “That won’t do at all. We must find it. I think the night wind might have borrowed it. It does love lovely sounds, and sometimes it forgets to bring them back.”

Together, Coco the kitten and Fern the flower elf began to follow the whispers of the wind. They asked a little cricket with shiny legs. “Excuse me, little cricket,” Fern asked politely. “Did you hear the happy song last night?”

“Chirp, chirp, not a peep,” the cricket answered, and polished one shiny leg as if that were all the news he had.

They rustled some friendly leaves. “Oh, leafy friends,” Coco meowed softly. “Did you see the happy song float by?”

The leaves whispered back, “Swoosh, swoosh, not a sign. But we heard a gentle sigh.”

Coco’s whiskers twitched. A branch creaked loudly above them. She wished she was back in her meadow, safe and sound. Fern just smiled. Her smile was like a warm ray of sunshine. She gently patted Coco’s paw. “We’re being very careful, Coco,” she said softly. Coco felt a little bit better, like a warm blanket was wrapped around her. They walked on, past a toadstool that held a bead of last night’s rain.

Suddenly Fern pointed with a tiny delicate finger. “Look. Over there.”

On a shimmering spiderweb, strung between two tall blades of grass, was a perfect round dewdrop. Inside the dewdrop they could see the faint beautiful notes of the happy song. It sparkled like a thousand tiny rainbows, all dancing together. It was all safe and sound, like little musical notes swimming in a tiny glass ball.

“The night wind tucked it there,” Fern said, her eyes wide with delight. “It thought it was such a pretty tune, it wanted to keep it safe.”

The night wind, bless its breezy heart, was known to be a little forgetful. It meant well, but sometimes it got carried away. To get the happy song back, they had to make a deal. Coco, the little kitten, had to let the night wind borrow her very favourite cozy nap spot in the meadow. The one where the sunbeams made the warmest, softest patches of gold. She had to let it borrow it for one whole night.

Coco imagined the cool air in her special spot. Her best sunny spot. It was a little bit sad to think about giving it up. She felt a little pang, like a tiny bee had landed on her heart. But if the other flowers could wake up and smile, and the mice could scurry happily to their beds, she would do it. “I’ll do it,” Coco meowed. Her voice was firm and clear, like a little bell ringing.

So Fern carefully helped Coco carry the dewdrop, with the happy song safe inside, back to the meadow. The night wind, a gentle soft sigh all around them, promised to keep Coco’s nap spot nice and cozy, like a warm hug. And it promised to bring it back by morning, good as new. As the happy song began to float from the dewdrop, a gentle soothing song sweeter than honey, the flowers perked up. Their petals unfurled like happy flags. The mice scurried happily to their homes. Their little tails wagged with relief. A butterfly that had been waiting on a stem opened its wings as if the music had been a door.

Coco snuggled into a different spot. It was a little less sunny, but still soft and peaceful. She had gone into the woods. She had asked the wind. She had helped all her friends. She closed her eyes. She listened to the sweet familiar happy song that now filled the entire meadow. And she drifted off to sleep. She dreamed of sunbeams, friendly wind whispers, and the happy sight of smiling flowers. Her purr was a soft rumble of happiness, and in the morning the gold patch would be hers again, smelling faintly of night and clover.
